entry: Original OTLP logging, tracing and metrics exporters → HTTP collector

questions.history: Set only common endpoint, `management.opentelemetry.otlp.compression=gzip` and common header `suite=common`.
questions.prediction: The parent lacks these common settings. On the merge expect HTTP requests to `/v1/logs`, `/v1/traces` and `/v1/metrics` at that collector, with `suite=common` and gzip bodies containing the corresponding signal.
questions.basis: The issue asks for one shared base. Pinned tests check the signal suffixes, exporter header configuration and HTTP compression. Decoding the request verifies that its declared encoding matches its body.
questions.refutation: Any signal misses the selected collector, uses the wrong path, loses the header, or advertises gzip for an undecodable body.

omit.parent: The original exporter does not recognize the common collector endpoint. Both pins run the explicit-endpoint control against the private recorder.

questions.history: Give logs an explicit `management.opentelemetry.logging.export.otlp.endpoint` ending in `/explicit`, omit common settings and leave compression at its HTTP default.
questions.prediction: Both revisions should send `Hello` to `/explicit` as uncompressed protobuf.
questions.basis: The existing HTTP integration test checks the exporter’s content type, absent content encoding and payload.
questions.refutation: A suffix is appended to the explicit endpoint, or the collector cannot read the logged body there.

questions.history: Retain the common endpoint, gzip and `suite=common`. Override only log compression to `none` and log header `suite` to `logs`, then emit the same log, span and metric.
questions.prediction: On the merge the log request should carry `suite=logs` once and have an uncompressed body. The trace and metric requests should retain common gzip and `suite=common`.
questions.basis: A per-signal override must leave the other exporters’ effective settings intact. Three independently captured requests expose accidental mutation of shared headers or defaults.
questions.refutation: A sibling request inherits a logs-only override, log headers contain both values, or the logged payload requires gzip to read.

omit.parent: This prediction concerns overrides of the merged common endpoint.
